One advantage of the method is that noncentral chi-square samples can be generated for a whole range of values of degrees of freedom using the same Chebyshev coefficients. This property is especially useful in model calibration. The squared Bessel process is a building block for the well-known Cox-Ingersoll-Ross (CIR) processes, which can be generated from squared Bessel processes through time change and linear transformation. Our direct inversion method thus allows the efficient and accurate simulation of these processes, which are used as models in a wide variety of applications.
item.dc:creator: Simon J. A. Malham, Anke Wiese, Yifan Xu

item.title: Upper bound on heat kernels of finite particle systems of Keller-Segel type
item.description: arXiv:2508.10892v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We obtain an upper bound on the heat kernel of the finite particle approximation of the Keller-Segel model of chemotaxis. The proof exploits a connection with certain non-local operators. We also obtain upper heat kernel bounds for related systems of interacting Brownian and stable particles that exhibit similar local blow-up effects.
item.dc:creator: S. E. Boutiah, D. Kinzebulatov

item.title: Separation properties of a hybrid point process with determinantal radii and uniform arguments
item.description: arXiv:2601.01474v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We recently characterized the almost sure separation of determinantal point processes $\Lambda_\phi$ in the plane associated with Fock spaces $\mathcal F_\phi$ with doubling weights $\phi$. We also showed that, as expected, a more restrictive condition is required to characterize the almost surely separated Poisson processes with the same first intensity as $\Lambda_\phi$. To gain further insight into this difference in behavior, we focus on radial weights $\phi$ and introduce a hybrid process $\Lambda_\phi^M=\{r_j e^{i\theta_j}\}_{j}$, where the moduli $r_j$ are taken from $\Lambda_\phi$, while the arguments $\theta_j$ are chosen independently and uniformly in $[0,2\pi)$, independently of the radii. Our main result is that the hybrid process is almost surely separated under exactly the same condition as the corresponding Poisson process. Thus, despite preserving the joint radial distribution of the determinantal process, independent angular randomization destroys its improved separation properties.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppe Lamberti, Xavier Massaneda

item.title: Combining e-values using demi-supermartingales
item.description: arXiv:2603.10329v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a new method for combining e-variables through demi-supermartingales, which settles an old conjecture in the literature on nonparametric mean testing. It also provides an explicit concentration bound for a certain Kullback--Leibler-type statistic arising in the stochastic multi-armed bandit literature. All of these combination results hold for independent e-variables as well as for the class of co-valid e-variables, whose dependence structure lies somewhere between independence and sequential validity. The results are further generalized to compound e-variables. The proofs proceed by analyzing elementary symmetric polynomials and their behavior as nonnegative demi-supermartingales.
item.dc:creator: Jiahao Ming, Aaditya Ramdas, Yi Shen, Ruodu Wang, Ian Waudby-Smith

item.title: Nonlinear Information Theory: Characterizing Distributional Uncertainty in Communication Models with Sublinear Expectation
item.description: arXiv:2603.16700v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A mathematical framework for information-theoretic analysis is established, with a new viewpoint of describing transmitted messages and communication channels by the nonlinear expectation theory, beyond classical probability framework. Based on nonlinear expectation theory, in this paper we define several fundamental concepts, such as nonlinear information entropy, nonlinear joint entropy, and nonlinear mutual information, and establish their basic properties. By using strong law of large numbers under sublinear expectations, we propose a nonlinear source coding theorem, which shows that nonlinear entropy is a sufficient achievability threshold for the achievable coding rate of uncertain-distribution sources under the maximum error probability criterion, and determines a cluster point of the achievable coding rate under the minimum error probability criterion. We also propose a nonlinear channel coding theorem, providing explicit expressions of the upper bound and a cluster point under the maximum and minimum error probability criterion, respectively, for the achievable coding rate of uncertain-distribution channels. Additionally, we propose a nonlinear rate-distortion source coding theorem, proving that the rate-distortion function based on nonlinear mutual information is a cluster point of the lossy compression performance of uncertain-distribution sources under the minimum expected distortion criterion. Finally, we show some examples and simulations to consolidate our theoretic study.
item.dc:creator: Wen-Xuan Lang, Shaoshi Yang, Jianhua Zhang, Zhiming Ma

item.title: An inversion formula for the 2-body interaction given the correlation functions
item.description: arXiv:2604.14681v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a classical gas described by the truncated correlation functions of all orders, we prove convergence of an expansion of the pair interaction part of the (unknown) potential in terms of the truncated correlation functions of all orders, at infinite volume.
item.dc:creator: Fabio Frommer, Tobias Kuna, Dimitrios Tsagkarogiannis

item.title: Counting connected multitype graphs with prescribed edge counts
item.description: arXiv:2606.17912v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine the exponential asymptotics of the number of connected labelled graphs with finitely many vertex types, prescribed numbers of vertices of each type, and prescribed edge counts between each pair of types. Under an irreducibility and strict surplus condition, we express the count for linear surplus of edges as the unrestricted count multiplied by an explicit exponential connectivity factor, up to a multiplicative error \(\exp\{o(n)\}\). The factor is characterized by a finite-dimensional nonlinear system whose solution exists and is unique. We use a probabilistic method, exploiting large-deviation principles and asymptotic estimates for connectedness probabilities to relate the counting problem to the emergence of giant components in suitably tuned supercritical random graphs. For connected bipartite graphs, we determine the exponential rate throughout the regime of positive linear excess and fixed positive limiting proportions of the two vertex classes. In the parameter ranges where the existing upper and lower bounds apply, this identifies the exponential rate left undetermined by those estimates.
item.dc:creator: Luisa Andreis, Mario Veshaj

item.title: Debiased parametric inference for regime-switching jump diffusions with infinite variation jumps
item.description: arXiv:2606.31057v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study high-frequency inference for an ergodic regime-switching jump diffusion with locally stable infinite-variation jumps. The state and the finite-state regime are observed on the same grid. The mesh satisfies \(h_n\to0\), while the horizon satisfies \(T_n=nh_n\to\infty\). We estimate structural drift and diffusion parameters in the presence of unknown regime-specific L\'evy measures. For a common activity index \(1<\beta<8/5\), we remove two leading jump biases from each regime's truncated variation. We then combine the diffusion estimator with estimated signed tail means in an adaptive drift contrast. We prove joint asymptotic normality at rates \(\sqrt{T_n}\) and \(\sqrt n\), together with feasible studentization. The growing horizon requires uniform control of the debiasing remainders and random denominators over increasing regime exposures. It also produces an explicit L\'evy-measure term in the drift covariance. A fixed-grid median stabilizes the two-step correction without changing its first-order limit. We study finite-sample behavior by simulation and apply the method to 127.5 hours of cattle sensor data. In the application, jaw-activity labels are recorded by a device separate from the sensor that measures the state process.
item.dc:creator: Yuzhong Cheng

item.title: Nonlinear Exchange Dynamics for Independent Sets
item.description: arXiv:2607.29016v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In recent years, nonlinear dynamics derived from kinetic theory have gained attention in the context of sampling configurations of spin systems such as the Ising model. We focus on nonlinear dynamics for the hard-core model, a canonical spin system with hard constraints that specifies a distribution over independent sets in a graph, weighted by their sizes. We explore two distinct types of nonlinear dynamics: the mean-field dynamics, which preserves the density (or average size) of independent sets, and the single-site dynamics, which preserves the marginal vector (i.e., the occupancy probabilities of the vertices). These dynamics are natural stochastic processes for sampling from the hard-core model with a specified density or marginal vector, respectively, both of which are canonical instances of maximum entropy distributions that have been studied in various contexts. In contrast to linear Markov chains, there is a significant lack of a fundamental theoretical framework for nonlinear dynamics. We develop foundational theoretical tools for analyzing nonlinear dynamics within the context of the hard-core model. We establish almost linear convergence of both the mean-field and single-site dynamics at sufficiently low density through novel coupling arguments. We also establish exponential decay of relative entropy for the mean-field dynamics all the way up to the critical density. Additionally, we design new algorithms for sampling from the hard-core distribution with either a specified density or a specified marginal vector. These algorithms are based on a related linear Markov chain, called the particle-system dynamics and inspired by the so-called Kac's program, that approximates the associated nonlinear dynamics. As we demonstrate in the paper, they are comparable in time complexity, but simpler to implement, than traditional approaches based on learning parameter values.
item.dc:creator: Mehrad Abbaszadeh Minab, Pietro Caputo, Zongchen Chen, Mario Morellini, Alistair Sinclair

item.title: Optimal Selling of Defaultable Assets using the Distribution Builder
item.description: arXiv:2608.21716v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider the problem of when it is best to sell a risky asset in the \textit{distribution builder} framework under the consideration of potential ruin. This approach allows investors to express their preferences directly as a desired target distribution without first specifying a risk aversion or utility function. Mathematically, the problem is closely related to the Skorokhod embedding problem of attaining a given distribution by stopping a diffusion process. We work in a general framework of one-dimensional diffusion processes and extend existing results to include the possibility of ruin. We first provide a full characterization of the set of distributions that can be attained before ruin occurs. Then, we formulate two optimization problems that tackle the issue of what to do if the originally specified distribution is either not attainable or not optimal: finding the attainable distribution closest to an unattainable distribution and selecting an optimal attainable distribution under first-order stochastic dominance constraints if the originally specified distribution is attainable, but not optimal. We provide sufficient conditions for the existence and uniqueness of solutions to these constrained convex optimization problems in an extended \(f\)-divergence framework, provide an analytic characterization of the solutions, and present numerical examples.
item.dc:creator: Sixian Jin, Stephan Sturm

item.title: A General Kernel Framework for Non-CND Distance Measures Using |D|-Dimensional Sparse Landmark Embeddings
item.description: arXiv:2609.19083v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Kernel methods, and Gaussian Processes (GPs) in particular, require a Hilbertian distance measure---one whose square is conditionally negative definite (CND)---to guarantee positive semi-definiteness (PSD) of the kernel matrix; a condition that fails for many natural input spaces, including smooth manifolds and spaces of probability distributions. We propose the Sparse Landmark Embedding (SLE) kernel, which eliminates this requirement entirely. Each input is embedded into a sparse feature vector via compactly supported bump functions centered at all |D| training points; applying any standard PSD kernel in this embedding space yields a kernel that is provably PSD for arbitrary distance measures. The compact support automatically controls embedding sparsity, keeping kernel matrices well-conditioned and computationally tractable despite the high ambient dimension. We provide theoretical guarantees on PSD, sparsity, stability, and universal approximation, and show that the SLE kernel matches or substantially exceeds domain-specific baselines in both predictive accuracy and uncertainty quantification using geodesic and Wasserstein distances.
item.dc:creator: Marcus M. Noack, Maher B. Alghalayini, Mark D. Risser

item.title: Percolation in the Stochastic Block Model
item.description: arXiv:2609.27141v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The stochastic block model is a paradigmatic model of networks with community structure. Yet percolation in the model has been studied primarily in cases with a fixed block structure, even though in real networks, the community structure may evolve as the network grows. Here we study percolation in sequences of stochastic block models in which the numbers and sizes of communities, as well as the intra- and intercommunity connection probabilities may all change with the network size. We analyze five such sequences using two methods: linearized self-consistent equations for the locally tree-like models and a branching process at the community scale for the models with nonvanishing clustering. We find that the critical average degree is not generally equal to $1$, even in locally tree-like sequences, because the transition depends on how connections are distributed across the evolving community structure. We also show that the community-scale branching process accurately predicts the transition when intercommunity connections are sufficiently sparse, even in the presence of nonvanishing clustering, while a geometric stochastic block model sequence demonstrates the limitations of this method when correlations between intercommunity connections cannot be neglected. These results extend percolation studies in the stochastic block model to more realistic scenarios with evolving community structure, and may provide new methods to derive the upper and lower bounds for the percolation threshold in geometric long-range percolation.
item.dc:creator: Luca Pieleanu, Moritz Laber, Narayan G. Sabhahit, Dmitri Krioukov

item.title: Localization near the edge for the lattice Anderson-Bernoulli model on general dimension
item.description: arXiv:2609.30209v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Anderson tight-binding model is a fundamental model of quantum transport and localization in disordered media. Solving a problem left open by Bourgain and Kenig, this paper proves Anderson localization near the bottom of the spectrum for the lattice Anderson model with Bernoulli potential, in any dimension $d\ge 2$. The proof uses the multiscale framework of Fr\"ohlich-Spencer and Bourgain-Kenig, and the main new ingredient is a probabilistic discrete unique continuation principle (PDUC) for the discrete Schr\"odinger equation. This PDUC is established via a bootstrap argument and a key probabilistic lemma proved by adaptively revealing the random potential.
item.dc:creator: Linjun Li, Shihe Liu, Lingfu Zhang

item.title: On the foundations of logic and probability, II. Modal probability spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.17049v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A class of models which brings to the fore the inner logic of the calculus of probability instead of assigning probabilities to sentences is introduced and investigated.
item.dc:creator: Loic Cosyns

item.title: Narrow escape problems beyond spherical holes: slits and tubes
item.description: arXiv:2610.26514v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The narrow escape problem consists in characterizing the exit event of a Brownian motion trapped inside a domain with reflecting boundary and small absorbing holes. Using recent advances in the quasi-stationary distribution approach, we first give an explicit set of hypotheses that allows one to derive the asymptotics of the exit time and of the exit hole distribution. We then apply it in dimension three to several hole shapes: spherical holes, thin spheroidal holes shrinking to curves on the boundary (slits), and holes located at the end of thin tubes attached to the domain. We illustrate the accuracy of the results with numerical simulations, and extend them to higher dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Louis Carillo
